title: Y Combinator-backed AI startup LemonLime promised interviews to 7 people who got company tattoos — then apologized
excerpt: This tattoo job interview stunt didn’t stick, but the criticism did.
content_html:
Brian O’Connell

Mon, August 3, 2026 at 10:30 AM MST 5 min read

A Silicon Valley company crossed a labor line last week after promising job interviews to candidates who agreed to stamp themselves with a permanent company tattoo.

Jordan Zietz, the CEO and cofounder of Y Combinator-backed AI startup LemonLime, based in San Francisco, issued the challenge for employment posts in the company's AI data and engineering slots, with seven job-seekers agreeing to the stunt at a late July corporate afterparty.

Must Read

  • Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

  • Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

  • Millionaires under 43 hold only 25% of their wealth in stocks. Here's where their money is actually going

At first, Zietz boasted about the tattoo challenge, sharing in a since-deleted LinkedIn Post: "We are bold, we take risks, and we do things that haven't been done before."

Zietz didn't stop there, following up with another post.

"Being committed to our mission is paramount," he wrote. "Pre-requisites for building the future. If you're reaching out to us to apply for a job, you might want to take notes."

Backlash erupted after the posts went public.

"I am DISGUSTED at this founder's behavior… The commodification of humans by an AI company is just too on-point," noted one LinkedIn post.

Before long, Zietz reappeared with a July 30 LinkedIn apology.

"I messed up," he stated. "At our YC afterparty, we offered free tattoos and said we'd be happy to interview anyone who got one. What I thought would be a fun, memorable way to meet people was, in reality, reckless, and instead came across as tying a permanent tattoo to a job opportunity, which showed poor judgment."

Zietz also added that the post was removed and the interviewees were contacted and assured they would receive a LemonLime job interview with no strings or tattoos attached.

"We're also ready to cover associated removal costs with anyone facing any delayed regret. I'm sorry to the people we put in that position, and to everyone who expected better from me," he added. "There's no clever explanation here. I got carried away, and I was wrong. For the facts: Interviews were available to everyone regardless."

The tattoo incident may say more about startup culture or today's job market

Workplace experts say a founder who believed people might permanently tattoo a company logo for an interview opportunity may have a point, if ill-delivered. They also say the stunt reveals the dark underside of the current hiring environment, particularly for young professionals trying to break into AI and tech.

content_html_zh:
布莱恩·奥康奈尔

2026 年 8 月 3 日星期一上午 10:30（MST） 阅读 5 分钟

上周，一家硅谷公司承诺为同意在自己身上贴上永久公司纹身的候选人提供面试机会，从而触犯了劳工界线。

Y Combinator 支持的位于旧金山的人工智能初创公司 LemonLime 的首席执行官兼联合创始人乔丹·齐茨 (Jordan Zietz) 在该公司的人工智能数据和工程职位上发布了招聘职位的挑战，七名求职者在 7 月底的公司余兴派对上同意了这一噱头。

必读

  • 杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 支持一个平台，让任何人都可以以低至 100 美元的价格投资出租房屋——无需真正成为房东即可像房东一样积累财富的 6 种方法
  • 戴夫·拉姆齐 (Dave Ramsey) 警告说，近 50% 的美国人正在犯一个重大的社会保障错误。 这就是它的本质以及尽快修复它的 3 个简单步骤
  • 43岁以下的百万富翁仅将其财富的25%投资于股票。 这就是他们的钱实际去向的地方

起初，齐茨吹嘘纹身挑战，并在一篇后来被删除的 LinkedIn 帖子中分享道：“我们很大胆，我们敢于冒险，我们做以前从未做过的事情。”

齐茨并没有就此止步，他又发了一篇帖子。

“致力于我们的使命至关重要，”他写道。 “建设未来的先决条件。 如果您联系我们申请工作，您可能需要做笔记。”

帖子公开后，引发了强烈反对。

“我对这位创始人的行为感到厌恶...... 人工智能公司将人类商品化实在是太切题了，”LinkedIn 的一篇帖子指出。

不久之后，Zietz 再次出现，并于 7 月 30 日在 LinkedIn 上道歉。

“我搞砸了，”他说。 “在我们的 YC 余兴派对上，我们提供免费纹身，并表示我们很乐意采访任何有纹身的人。 我以为这是一种有趣、令人难忘的结识他人的方式，但实际上是鲁莽的，反而给人留下了将永久纹身与工作机会联系在一起的印象，这表明我的判断力很差。”

齐茨还补充说，该帖子已被删除，并联系了受访者并保证他们将接受 LemonLime 的面试，不附带任何条件或纹身。

“我们还准备好为任何面临延迟遗憾的人支付相关的搬迁费用。 我对我们安排在这个职位上的人以及所有对我有更好期望的人感到抱歉，”他补充道。 “这里没有聪明的解释。 我得意忘形了，我错了。 事实上：无论如何，每个人都可以接受采访。”

纹身事件可能更多地说明了创业文化或当今的就业市场

职场专家表示，一位相信人们可能会为了面试机会而永久纹身公司标志的创始人，如果表达得不好，可能是有道理的。 他们还表示，这一噱头揭示了当前招聘环境的黑暗面，特别是对于试图闯入人工智能和科技领域的年轻专业人士而言。
